The steps include: Define Problem, Get Data, Prepare Data, Train Model, and Deploy Model. • Using the ML Toolkit framework, developed and demonstrated data-driven process controls in real full-scale facilities for five promising Applications (water resource recovery facility process technologies) that provide a whole plant approach and offer substantial energy and resource recovery benefits. • Conducted a life cycle assessment (LCA) and a techno-economic analysis (TEA) to quantify the benefits realized from implementation of each application in this project compared to a relevant conventional baseline scenario. These two analyses demonstrated the benefits from both a holistic sustainability perspective as well as an economic perspective. • Developed an ML Toolkit (i.e., website) to support the development and training of wastewater process engineers and others to enable more broad-scale implementation of ML solutions. The ML Toolkit walks users through each step of the ML Toolkit framework and demonstrates the steps through the five case study applications. Each case study includes a link to access the project code via a Google Colab notebook, a short project overview video, and a code walk-through video. • Summarized ML implementation considerations and lessons learned for each of the five case study applications as well as the project overall. The lessons learned will guide those considering embarking on a data-driven controls approach at their utility or in their business so they can avoid unexpected challenges or reinventing the wheel.
